pr_title: Fix `RESTWithNext` error type, repairing `gh status` and attestation retries
pr_body:
## Description

The `api.Client.RESTWithNext` method did not handle errors in the same way as `api.Client.REST`. The latter wrapped the `go-gh` error into a new `api` error and the former simply returned it. From an error message point of view, there was no visible difference but programmatic checks for `errors.As(err, &api.HTTPError{})` would be true for `REST` and false for `RESTWithNext`.

I cannot find any reason for this to have been intentional. I suspect what happened was that `RESTWithNext` previously used to handle this case via the following removed code:

```go
	success := resp.StatusCode >= 200 && resp.StatusCode < 300
	if !success {
		return "", HandleHTTPError(resp)
	}
```

But at some point `go-gh` was created, and the `go-gh` api client `Request`/`RequestWithContext` methods began returning errors for non success http status codes.

This broke two behaviours:
 * `gh status` is supposed to gracefully degrade if notifications or events are inaccessible.
 * `gh attestation` commands is supposed to retry attestation fetching for 500 status codes.

## Notes

This is a prerequisite for consolidating GitHub API URL derivation onto `api.Client` (part of the groundwork for per-host API routing, #13717 / #13760), but it is a user-facing bugfix in its own right and is worth reviewing as such.
commit_message:
Merge pull request #13988 from cli/williammartin-fix-restwithnext-error-type
Fix `RESTWithNext` error type, repairing `gh status` and attestation retries
task_text:
Fix the error returned when a paginated GitHub API request fails with a non-success HTTP status. Today, these failures return a raw transport-library error, while standard API requests return the CLI's own HTTP error type. The two differ in type even though their messages look the same, so any caller that checks for the HTTP error type gets a false result on the paginated path.

This breaks two behaviours. The status command should tolerate an inaccessible notifications or events endpoint and keep rendering the rest of its output, but it currently fails. The attestation commands should retry fetching attestations when the server responds with a 500 status, but they currently do not retry.

After the fix, a failed paginated request should produce the same error type as a standard request, with the same status code and scope guidance. The status command should degrade gracefully on a 404 from those endpoints, and attestation fetching should retry on a 500.

+	reg := &httpmock.Registry{}

+			Request:    req,
+			StatusCode: http.StatusNotFound,
+			Body:       io.NopCloser(bytes.NewBufferString(`{"message": "Not Found"}`)),
+			Header: http.Header{
+				"Content-Type":            {"application/json"},
+				"X-Accepted-Oauth-Scopes": {"repo"},
+				"X-Oauth-Scopes":          {"read:user"},

type testHostConfig string

func (c testHostConfig) DefaultHost() (string, string) {
	return string(c), ""
}

func TestNewCmdStatus(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		cli   string
		wants StatusOptions
	}{
		{
			name: "defaults",
		},
		{
			name: "org",
			cli:  "-o cli",
			wants: StatusOptions{
				Org: "cli",
			},
		},
		{
			name: "exclude",
			cli:  "-e cli/cli,cli/go-gh",
			wants: StatusOptions{
				Exclude: []string{"cli/cli", "cli/go-gh"},
			},
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		ios, _, _, _ := iostreams.Test()
		ios.SetStdinTTY(true)
		ios.SetStdoutTTY(true)

		if tt.wants.Exclude == nil {
			tt.wants.Exclude = []string{}
		}

		f := &cmdutil.Factory{
			IOStreams: ios,
			Config: func() (gh.Config, error) {
				return config.NewBlankConfig(), nil
			},
		}
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			argv, err := shlex.Split(tt.cli)
			assert.NoError(t, err)

			var gotOpts *StatusOptions
			cmd := NewCmdStatus(f, func(opts *StatusOptions) error {
				gotOpts = opts
				return nil
			})
			cmd.SetArgs(argv)
			cmd.SetIn(&bytes.Buffer{})
			_, err = cmd.ExecuteC()
			assert.NoError(t, err)

			assert.Equal(t, tt.wants.Org, gotOpts.Org)
			assert.Equal(t, tt.wants.Exclude, gotOpts.Exclude)
		})
	}
}
